To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 12‐month diet and/or exercise lifestyle‐intervention in overweight‐to‐ obese postmenopausal white women resulted in significant weight loss and improvements in adiposity, with a combination of diet plus exercise being the most effective.
the combination of diet and exercise is more effective than either diet or exercise alone for weight loss and body fat reduction in sedentary, overweight‐to‐ obese postmenopausal white women.

a 1‐year lifestyle intervention consisting of a calorie‐restricted, low‐fat eating plan and a moderate‐intervention exercise program, alone or combined, is effective in reducing body weight and adipose tissue in overweight‐to‐ obese postmenopausal white women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diet and exercise, alone or combined, on weight and body composition in postmenopausal, overweight‐to‐ obese women.
the effects of diet and exercise on body composition in overweight‐to‐ obese postmenopausal, sedentary women.
the effects of diet and exercise on body weight and body composition in overweight‐to‐ obese postmenopausal, sedentary women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

lifestyle intervention involving diet and/or exercise, alone or combined, over 1 year, improves body weight and body composition in overweight‐to‐ obese postmenopausal, sedentary women, with the greatest changes occurring in those receiving both diet and exercise.
a calorie‐restricted diet and moderate‐intensity exercise, alone and in combination, are effective interventions to reduce body weight and adipose mass in postmenopausal overweight women.

the combination of a calorie‐restricted low‐fat diet and moderate‐intensity aerobic exercise is the most effective lifestyle intervention for weight loss in overweight‐to‐ obese postmenopausal females.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined diet plus exercise lifestyle intervention was the most successful in achieving weight loss and fat mass reduction.
the combined diet and exercise intervention produced the greatest change in body composition.
the combination of a reduced‐fat diet with exercise is the most effective lifestyle‐based intervention for weight loss among overweight‐to‐ obese postmenopausal white women.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combined intervention of diet and exercise is more efficacious than either alone for improving body weight and adipose mass among postmenopausal, overweight‐to‐ obese women.
a combination of diet and exercise, even when done at a relatively low intensity, results in the greatest weight and fat loss.
a calorie‐restricted diet, aerobic exercise program, or a combination of both interventions are all effective for weight loss in overweight‐to‐ obese postmenopausal, sedentary women.
